questions.statement: Summer is the time of year ________ many people go on vacation.

options.feedback: Correct! "When" is the relative adverb for time.

questions.explanation:
Usamos el adverbio relativo "when" para dar más información sobre un momento o periodo de tiempo mencionado anteriormente.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: The reason ________ I'm calling you is to invite you to my birthday party.

options.feedback: Correct! "Why" is used after the word "reason" to explain a cause.

questions.explanation:
"Why" es el adverbio relativo que utilizamos para explicar la razón o el motivo de algo, usualmente después de la palabra "reason".

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Bogotá, ________ is the capital of Colombia, is a very large city.
questions.context: Non-defining relative clause about a city.

options.feedback: Correct! We use "which" (not "that") in non-defining clauses for things/places.
Incorrect. "That" cannot be used after a comma in non-defining clauses.

questions.explanation:
En las oraciones de relativo explicativas (non-defining), que van entre comas y añaden información extra no esencial, debemos usar "which" para objetos o lugares, nunca "that".

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: My brother, ________ lives in London, is coming to visit us next week.

options.feedback: Correct! "Who" is used for people in both defining and non-defining clauses.
Incorrect. "That" cannot be used in non-defining clauses.

questions.explanation:
Para personas en oraciones explicativas (entre comas), el pronombre correcto es "who". Al igual que con objetos, no podemos usar "that" en este contexto.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Mr. Smith, ________ son is my best friend, is a very kind man.
questions.context: Relative clause with "whose" for non-defining information.

options.feedback: Correct! "Whose" shows possession in non-defining clauses too.

questions.explanation:
"Whose" se utiliza para indicar posesión o relación familiar, incluso en oraciones que proporcionan información adicional entre comas.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: 2010 was the year ________ Colombia celebrated its bicentennial of independence.

options.feedback: Correct! Referring to a specific year (time).

questions.explanation:
Al referirnos a un año específico como el marco temporal de un evento, el adverbio relativo "when" es el más adecuado.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence is a **non-defining** relative clause?

options.text: The car that I bought is blue.
My car, which I bought last month, is blue.
options.feedback: Correct! The commas and "which" show this is extra information.

options.text: The man who is standing there is my uncle.
This is the house where I live.

questions.explanation:
Las oraciones explicativas (non-defining) añaden información sobre algo que ya está identificado (por ejemplo, "mi carro" ya sabemos cuál es). Siempre llevan comas.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
Can we delete the relative pronoun in this sentence?
"My teacher, **who** is very strict, gave us a lot of homework."
questions.context: Deleting relative pronouns in non-defining clauses.

options.text: Yes, because it is the object.
Yes, because it's a non-defining clause.
No, relative pronouns in non-defining clauses can never be omitted.
options.feedback: Correct! This is a strict rule.

questions.explanation:
A diferencia de las oraciones especificativas (defining), en las explicativas (non-defining) **nunca** se puede omitir el pronombre relativo, incluso si funciona como objeto.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: He arrived two hours late, ________ made everyone very angry.

options.feedback: Correct! "Which" can refer to the entire previous idea or situation.

questions.explanation:
Un uso avanzado de "which" es referirse no solo a un sustantivo, sino a toda la situación descrita en la oración anterior. Siempre va precedido de una coma.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.context: Identifying punctuation errors in relative clauses.

options.text: My mother, who is a chef, loves spicy food.
The house where I was born is now a museum.
Albert Einstein that was a genius discovered relativity.
options.feedback: Correct! Error found. For a specific famous person, we need a non-defining clause with "who" and commas.

options.text: This is the reason why I didn't come.

questions.explanation:
Cuando hablamos de nombres propios únicos (como Einstein), la información adicional debe ir en una oración explicativa (comas + who/which), no una especificativa con "that".

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence is most suitable for a biography in a magazine?

options.text: Shakira is a singer that she is from Barranquilla.
Shakira, whose real name is Shakira Isabel Mebarak, has sold millions of albums.
options.feedback: Correct! Uses a non-defining clause to provide interesting extra details.

options.text: Shakira is a person who she sings very well.
The singer Shakira which lives in Miami is famous.

questions.explanation:
El uso de oraciones explicativas permite a los escritores (nivel B1/B2) entrelazar hechos biográficos de manera fluida y profesional.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
"I visited Cali. It is known as the salsa capital. I went there in December."
Choose the best combined sentence:
questions.context: Selecting the best combination of information.

options.text: In December, I visited Cali, which is known as the salsa capital.
options.feedback: Correct! It combines time, place, and extra information elegantly.

options.text: I visited Cali where is the salsa capital in December.
options.feedback: Incorrect. "Where" needs a subject after it or to be replaced by "which".

options.text: Cali, that is the salsa capital, was visited by me when December.
options.feedback: Incorrect. "That" cannot be used this way.

options.text: When December I visited Cali which it is salsa capital.

questions.explanation: Combinar múltiples piezas de información requiere el uso preciso de conectores temporales y oraciones de relativo explicativas para mantener la cohesión del texto.
